What's more dangerous: Getting hit by lightning mid-jump or getting hit by lightning with feet on the ground?
For a direct hit it's the same. But standing on the ground you can get hurt by a nearby hit.

The discharge path of lightning has traveled through high resistance air a very long way. I guarantee you a small gap between you and the ground will pose no significant resistance to it and you will be messed up either way.

I'm not sure of the overall balance; but one thing that is more dangerous when you jump (I think) is it increases the odds you'll be exposed to hot plasma on more than one part of your body (the entry and exit points; if you had your feet on the ground, the electricity would move thru without heating air.

I'm not sure if things change with lightining though; this is based on my personal experience messing with a broken plasma globe, where touching the spark midair hurts way more than touching the wire directly (don't try this at home, I'm an untrained idiot).
